R0176.title: Timestamp Dependence Attack
R0176.definition: Smart contracts rely on block timestamps for logic decisions; miners can manipulate timestamps to affect contract execution results.
R0176.description: Smart contracts often use block timestamps (block.timestamp) to implement time-related logic, such as lottery draws, option expiration, interest calculations, etc. Miners can freely set block timestamps within a certain range (typically 15 seconds). Attackers can exploit this feature to manipulate contract results, such as selecting favorable draw times, triggering early or delaying execution, etc.
R0176.influence: Contract logic manipulated, lottery results predictable, time-sensitive business fails.

observables: A smart contract uses block.timestamp as the key determinant for lottery draws or option expiration
The block timestamp is adjusted by a miner within a 15-second range before and after a contract's critical operation to a favorable value
Contract results dependent on timestamps deviate from randomness expectations, with the attacker repeatedly hitting favorable outcomes
Time-sensitive business (interest calculation, expiration settlement) produces anomalous execution results in specific blocks
